toolLimitation.reason: WALA does not model the implicit JVM-internal calls to ClassLoader.loadClass() that occur when executing 'new' bytecode instructions for classes that haven't been loaded yet. WALA treats 'new' instructions (SSANewInstruction) purely as object allocation operations without modeling the underlying class loading mechanism. This is a deliberate abstraction to focus on application-level control flow rather than JVM implementation details.

potentialTestCase.description: Create a minimal Java program with a static initializer that contains a 'new' instruction for a class. The static initializer in class A should instantiate class B using 'new B()'. At runtime, when A's <clinit> is executed, the JVM will implicitly call ClassLoader.loadClass("B") before executing the 'new' instruction. WALA's call graph will show the <clinit> method as reachable but will not include an edge from A.<clinit> to ClassLoader.loadClass().
